facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old woman was being monitored for a left ciliary body mass for 3 years presented with declining vision in her left eye
Her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/50 OS
Pupils, intraocular pressures, anterior chambers, and lenses were unremarkable in both eyes
a nasal mass posterior to the lens was evident, which had grown considerably in size since her last visit
Ophthalmoscopic examination showed a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity
Ultra-widefield imaging: White mass emanating anteriorly from the nasal ciliary body and protruding into the vitreous cavity
Vitreous aspirate cytology: Negative for malignant cells
Hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei
S100 (neural crest marker): Positive
Glial fibrillary acidic protein (astrocyte marker): Patchy positive
CD34 (fibroblast marker): Negative
Smooth muscle actin: Negative

Vitreous aspirate cytology: Negative for malignant cells

Glial fibrillary acidic protein (astrocyte marker): Patchy positive
CD34 (fibroblast marker): Negative
Smooth muscle actin: Negative

concepts.why: The presence of a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity, along with the histopathological findings of a hypovascular myxoid lesion, suggests a medulloepithelioma.
The patient's declining vision and the presence of a nasal mass posterior to the lens, which has grown in size, could be indicative of a ciliary body melanoma.
The positive S100 and patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein staining suggest a neuroepithelial origin for the tumor.
The patient's declining vision and the presence of a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity could be causing a retinal detachment.
The hypovascular myxoid lesion with positive S100 staining could be indicative of a uveal schwannoma.
The presence of a nasal mass posterior to the lens, which has grown in size, could be indicative of a ciliary body cyst.
The presence of a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity, along with the negative vitreous aspirate cytology, could be indicative of an intraocular lymphoma.
The patient's declining vision and the presence of a nasal mass posterior to the lens, which has grown in size, could be indicative of a choroidal melanoma.
The negative smooth muscle actin staining and positive S100 staining are consistent with a diagnosis of neurofibroma, which explains the smooth muscle actin negativity.

rationales.F06: Ultra-widefield imaging showing a white mass emanating from the nasal ciliary body is highly suggestive of a ciliary body tumor.
rationales.F07: Negative vitreous aspirate cytology rules out malignant cells, making medulloepithelioma and ciliary body melanoma less likely.
rationales.F08: Hypovascular myxoid lesion with spindle and stellate cells is consistent with a neuroepithelial tumor or uveal schwannoma.
rationales.F09: Positive S100 staining is consistent with a neuroepithelial tumor or uveal schwannoma.
rationales.F10: Patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein staining is consistent with a neuroepithelial tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a hypovascular myxoid lesion with S100 and glial fibrillary acidic protein positivity supports a neural crest origin, and the lack of contradictions makes Neuroepithelial tumor the most fitting diagnosis.
